gallery.title: File:Edinburgh Arthur Seat dsc06165.jpg
gallery.description:
Arthur's Seat, Edinburgh, viewed from Pollock Halls.  
1880s map of the park
Arthur's Seat, an extinct volcano and the highest point in Edinburgh, is at the centre of the park, with the cliffs of Salisbury Crags to the west. There are three lochs: St Margaret's Loch, Dunsapie Loch, and Duddingston Loch. The ruins of St Anthony's Chapel stand above St Margaret's Loch. Queen's Drive is the main route through the Park. St Margaret's Well and St Anthony's Well are both natural springs within the park. Holyrood Park is located to the south-east of the Old Town, at the edge of the city centre. Abbeyhill is to the north, and Duddingston village to the east. The University of Edinburgh's Pollock Halls of Residence are to the south-west, and Dumbiedykes is to the west.
Arthur's Seat is the remains of a now extinct volcano which rises 250 metres (823 feet) above Holyrood Park in Edinburgh.

gallery.title: File:Greyfriars Bobby 07.jpg
gallery.description: In 1873 Lady Burdett-Coutts commissioned a statue and fountain which was  erected at the southern end of the George IV Bridge to commemorate Greyfriars Bobby. Bobby was a Skye Terrier who reportedly spent 14 years guarding the grave of his owner, John Gray, until he died himself on 14 January 1872.

gallery.source: Scandic Crown Hotel, High Street - geograph.org.uk - 1343722
gallery.description: Scandic Crown Hotel, High Street An architectural tour de force, designed by Ian Begg and built in 1990, this building proves that it is possible to maintain the character of the High Street by borrowing stylistically from Scotland's traditional vernacular architecture when building anew. This hotel blends in harmoniously with the surrounding environment but still makes a bold impression in its own right.

gallery.description: In September 1745, Bonnie Prince Charlie held his council of war before the Battle of Prestonpans in this house which was a tavern in Duddingston Village. The Jacobite horse were camped on open land to the south of the village, now called Cavalry Park.
